analysis: multi-event re-evaluation of immutable saved traces
design_status: Post-hoc evaluator study, frozen before full-corpus re-evaluation; Ca_HVA case already known. Not a new independent confirmation.
scope: Both47geometries, both imposed/autonomous modes, all24cases, all3frozen seeds, all4arms, all nodes and11current channels;100/500/1000ms prefixes. Reuse immutable original voltage/calcium/gate/amplitude scores and native floors; recompute original timing exactly and substitute only the separately labelled multi-event timing/presence result.

definition.baseline_and_scale: Same original reference[0], S=max(max(abs(reference)),floor), reference transient A=max(abs(reference-reference[0])). Candidate uses the same reference baseline and threshold0.1*A; no candidate rescaling.
definition.eligibility: Preserve original global temporal eligibility: A>=0.25*S, A>=10*floor and reference global maximum is not at the window boundary. Unsupported/boundary timing is explicitly not_evaluable; original numerical current/state gates remain authoritative.
definition.events: An event is a maximal contiguous above-threshold excursion. Preserve one-sample events; no smoothing, hysteresis, minimum duration or gap merging. This is a threshold-episode evaluator, not a detector of every biological or subthreshold response.
definition.matching: Monotone one-to-one dynamic programming. Lexicographically maximize matched cardinality, then minimize the sum of peak_distance/0.2 + onset_distance/0.3 + offset_distance/0.3. No learned weights or new distance acceptance gate. With equal counts this is ordered pairing. Matching alone never implies a pass: every matched event must meet the original tolerances; missing and spurious episodes always fail. Equal-count deletion/insertion may be operationally labelled timing, not a causal identity claim.
definition.peak: Within each matched episode, same relative near-maximum band0.001 and nearest plateau-sample distance as the original evaluator. Use all matched episodes, not the best global peak.
definition.endpoints: Compare original sample-index onsets/offsets with0.3ms tolerance; record right-boundary offsets as censored lower bounds rather than complete physical offsets. No interpolation or relative time shifting.
definition.unsupported_reference: Do not invent event timing for absent/boundary reference transients. Record coverage explicitly. An unexpectedly large candidate transient on an amplitude-unsupported reference is a spurious-support failure if it meets the same0.25*S and10*floor eligibility requirements. Boundary-censored reference transients remain not_evaluable, not automatically spurious.
definition.amplitude: Do not normalize away amplitude errors or alter existing nrmse/nmax/charge/blocked-current/gate/voltage/calcium gates. Report support mismatch separately from temporal error.
definition.decision: Retain original143/144NO-GO. Produce separate original versus multi-event case counts, coverage, new failures/recoveries and event diagnostics. No automatic144/144,48authorization, biological-equivalence or speedup claim. A borderline reference episode absent from the candidate remains a presence failure, not waived.

negative_controls.synthetic: Identity, flat reference, plateau, exact timing boundary, just-outside-boundary delay, missing/spurious/split/merged episodes, scaling and sign error, single-sample borderline support, equal-count displaced response, boundary censoring. Known-bad controls must fail; allowed sub-tolerance timing and identity controls must pass.
negative_controls.saved_reference_mutants: For every unique supported47reference geometry/case/node/channel at1000ms: identity,1ms whole-trace delay, deletion of the first complete threshold episode, injection of an above-threshold single-sample episode in a quiet gap,1.5x transient-amplitude scaling. Report exclusions and observed rejection rates by control type; no selective filtering based on success. Mutants are diagnostics, never candidate training or model changes.
negative_controls.falsifier: Any identity failure or accepted validly constructed known-bad control invalidates the new evaluator study for qualification; report it rather than tuning on the full cohort.
